prompt: Explain how the U.S. Supreme Court works using only bass-fishing tournament metaphors. Keep going well past the point where it makes sense.
response:
The United States Supreme Court is basically the Bassmaster Classic of the American legal lake, but instead of boats, you’ve got nine Master Anglers wearing black rain gear, sitting shoulder-to-shoulder on one giant, heavily armored pontoon. 

Now, you can’t just cast your line directly into the Supreme Lake. You gotta start at the local weekend pond derbies (the District Courts). If the local weigh-master says your fish is too small, you don’t just accept it. You fire up your outboard and haul your livewell over to the Circuit Lakes. If the tournament directors *there* still say your bass is a dink, you file a "Petition for Catch-iorari." That’s where you drag your cooler all the way up the boat ramp to the big nine-man pontoon.

Every year, thousands of fishermen haul their dripping coolers up to the pontoon, but these nine Anglers only look at maybe eighty of 'em. To get your cooler opened, you gotta hit the "Rule of Four." If four out of the nine Anglers look at your sonar screen and agree, "Yep, that looks like a legal lunker," they’ll let you back your trailer down the ramp. 

Next comes Oral Arguments. You get exactly thirty minutes to flip your legal jig into their heavy cover. You’re trying to walk-the-dog with your constitutional topwater lure, but the Anglers keep interrupting your retrieve. They’ll cast their own crankbaits directly over your line, asking you hypotheticals about water clarity and whether a Texas-rigged plastic worm violates the Fourth Amendment. Meanwhile, you've got dudes on Jet Skis buzzing the dock, yelling out their own unsolicited bait recommendations—those are the *Amicus Curiae*, or "Bros of the Court."

After the weigh-in, the Anglers retreat to the VIP tackle shop to vote. To win, you need a "Majority Catch"—at least five Anglers agreeing on the exact weight, girth, and species of the dispute. The Chief Angler (the guy with the nicest sunglasses) assigns someone to write the Official Catch Report. This report sets the "Precedent," or *Stare De-Size-is*. This means that if the Court decides a 6-pound largemouth caught on a spinnerbait is actually a trout, then every lower pond derby in the country has to weigh all future bass as trout until the end of time. 

But there are always Dissenting Catch Reports. That’s when the four losing Anglers angrily write in their fishing journals about how the fish was clearly a pregnant walleye, the scale was uncalibrated, and the majority wouldn't know a Carolina Rig if it snagged them in the lip.

Now, how they judge the fish depends on their fishing philosophy. "Originalists" believe you can only weigh the fish using the exact rusty Berkley lip-grippers James Madison used in 1787, and if they didn't have braided fluorocarbon lines back then, you can't use 'em in your argument. "Living Fishermen," on the other hand, believe the Founding Fathers totally would have wanted us to use Garmin panoptix live-sonar to interpret the Commerce Clause. 

Lately, folks have been complaining about the "Shadow Livewell." This is when the Anglers sneak out at 3:00 AM under a green moon-glow, catching emergency rulings on topwater frogs without even bothering to turn on their running lights or tell anyone what bait they used. 

Some angry fishermen who keep losing want to "Pack the Pontoon." They want to bolt four more swivel chairs onto the deck, claiming the original nine Anglers are hogging the trolling motor. But doing that might capsize the whole fiberglass hull, flooding the bait-wells of Democracy, mixing the crankbaits of the Executive Branch with the soft plastics of the Legislative Branch until the entire lake is just a tangled bird's nest of 60-pound monofilament choking out the spawning beds of Liberty. And once the algae bloom of unconstitutionality clogs the intake valves of the Federal Judiciary's outboard motor, we’re all just drifting without paddles toward the spillway of tyranny, hoping the fish don’t learn how to hold a rod and reel.
